answer: A proof-of-replication membership rule derives a 1 GiB file from SHA-256(nebula || epoch) and seals a cipher replica per key using sequential memory-hard encoding. Each key must pass 12 random block-proof audits per hour within 2 seconds; a mirror sealed for another key is invalid. Extra rewarded keys need separate replicas or recomputation within that deadline. Verifiers must benchmark the encoding: fast regeneration of missing blocks defeats the claimed per-key storage cost.
